title: Quantile-bucketed KV memory sweep and p95 regression harness
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a reproducible load-test harness that uses quantile-aware request bucketing to measure KV/prefix cache behavior across a controlled memory budget sweep. The harness should produce tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, hit-rate, and memory-allocated tradeoff curves, and wire in an automatic regression detector that flags >5% p95 regressions against a rolling baseline.
goal: Understand how hit-rate curves translate to p95 tail latency and tokens/sec at multiple memory allocations for production-like sequence length mixes; provide an automated alerting rule and a dashboard tile for nightly regression checks.
success_criteria: Harness can run a full sweep (4 memory points x 6 load scenarios) in <6 hours on ci-bench machine
Automated regression detector runs post-sweep and emits a pass/fail artifact with p95 comparisons and effect sizes
Dashboard shows hit-rate vs p95 vs memory budget heatmap and tokens/sec trend for each scenario
Noise floor characterization completed: per-scenario p95 standard deviation <10% across 5 repeated runs
test_plan: Define 6 workload scenarios (chat-short, chat-long, codex, paraphrase-heavy, rerank-heavy, mixed) with real token length distributions sampled from telemetry
Implement quantile bucketing: split requests into buckets by prefix length and recent-KV-hotness to avoid averaging artifacts
Sweep memory allocations: 1GB, 2GB, 4GB, 8GB mapped to cache entries via current LRU sizing
For each memory point and scenario run a warmup phase (10k requests), main phase (200k requests) while measuring tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency per bucket, and hit-rate
Repeat each combination 3 times to estimate variance
Post-process to compute relative p95 change vs baseline and run a bootstrap-based regression detector (alpha=0.05) to reduce false positives
environment: ci-bench1 (A100-40GB on ubuntu22) with runtime-2.1 candidate build; KV cache feature flags: prefix_cache_v2=true, adaptive_prefetch=false
baseline_runs: Baseline uses build runtime-2.0 with current default LRU sizing; baseline sweep completed 2026-03-05 and stored at s3://bench-results/kvcache/baseline-2026-03-05
preliminary_results: Initial runs show non-linear p95 increase between 2GB and 4GB on chat-long scenario despite only modest hit-rate drop (from 78% to 72%). Tokens/sec remained stable until memory <2GB where throughput dropped 18%. Variance across repeats for p95 was 7-12% depending on scenario.
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Experiment harness skeleton checked in (bench/harness/quantile-bucket) - implemented request generator and basic metrics plumbing
2026-03-11: Integrated quantile bucketing and telemetry ingestion from anonymized traces; synthetic scenarios validated against sample traces
2026-03-12: Added memory allocation toggles and eviction counters; executed quick smoke for chat-short and codex scenarios
2026-03-13: Full sweep executed overnight; preliminary artifacts uploaded to s3 and basic postprocessing script produced heatmap PNGs
2026-03-14: Observed anomalous p95 bump in chat-long between 2GB->4GB; instrumented per-bucket KV latency to investigate (note added to blockers)
blockers: Inconsistent eviction counters reported by runtime at high concurrency - needs runtime-instrumentation patch (ENG-276821) to get accurate per-shard evictions
Dashboard tile requires a new aggregations endpoint from observability (PR open, see related_prs)
next_steps: Land runtime instrumentation patch and re-run targeted 2GB/4GB chat-long runs to validate the anomalous p95 behavior
Wire regression detector output into nightly CI and set threshold to alert the oncall Slack channel with links to artifacts
Add adaptive_prefetch=true scenario to quantify benefits across memory budgets
Publish a short findings note and recommend default memory footprint guidance for chat-long workloads
notes: This ticket focuses on measurement fidelity. Avoid tuning LRU heuristics in this run; follow-up ticket will evaluate algorithmic mitigations once measurement artifact is confirmed. Keep raw traces for 30 days. If regression detector flags a failure, escalate to oncall and attach the smallest failing trace subset for triage.
